title: When he failed
hookLine: he confessed his fault and went back to God without fuss
tomorrow: can a two-second prayer in the middle of a shift count?

cards: Eleven at night, lights off, and the replay starts. The thing you said at work. The look on their face.
You run it again with a better line, then again, then you version an apology you'll never send. In a monastery kitchen, a cook called Brother Lawrence slips up too. He admits it freely.
But the visitor who wrote down their conversations noticed how short his response was. No replay. No trial in his head.
So what did he do instead?

teach.b: First, he admits it. Lawrence never claims he stopped failing. When he fell short in his duty, the visitor records, he simply confessed his fault to God.

Second, the sentence. As it was written down, it runs something like this: I'll never do otherwise if you leave me to myself; it's you who must keep me from falling, and mend what is wrong. Not a vow to try harder.
An admission that he can't fix himself alone. Third, the part that's easy to skip.

After that, he gave himself no further uneasiness about it. In another conversation he says he was very aware of his faults but not discouraged by them; he confessed them to God and didn't plead to excuse them.
Fourth, the return. Having confessed, he went back in peace to his usual practice of love and adoration.
Back to the pans. Here's the thing to tell a friend tonight: Lawrence didn't turn his faults into a project.
He turned each one into a sentence. This isn't the sacrament of confession, which Catholics also seek. It's the quick turn inside an ordinary day, between the slip and the next task.

how: Catholics have short acts of contrition that can be said in the middle of a day when a fault is noticed, and the sacrament of confession, where sins are brought to a priest.

o: a story about the day Lawrence quit the kitchen
Lawrence's way: confess a fault, then return to God
a rule that monks must never admit their faults

games.q: when he failed — tap the pairs.
p: left to God, not to himself

s: no fuss means Lawrence didn't much care about his faults
he was very aware of them. he confessed each one; he just didn't stall on it.
Lawrence said he eventually stopped failing
he speaks plainly of failing in his duty and confessing it.
after confessing, he gave himself no further uneasiness
he went back in peace to his practice of love and adoration.

games.q: your friend forgot to pick up her little brother, who waited an hour. two days later she's still apologizing every time she sees him. by Lawrence's way, what's next?
o: keep apologizing until he finally says it's fine.
act like it never happened, so nobody feels awkward.
own it once, plainly, and be on time next week.
games.why: Lawrence confessed his fault in a sentence and gave himself no further uneasiness. owning it is the point; the endless replay isn't.

practice: Bring one small slip from this week to mind. Say it out loud once, plainly, in a single sentence, with no defense attached.
Then come back to your breath, and each time the replay starts, return the way Lawrence returned to his pans: without a speech.

wordCard.voice: When he failed. Lawrence's way with his own faults: own it, hand the mending to God, and go back to love.

carryVoice: Your line: no fuss. A slip, a sentence, and back to the stove. See you tomorrow.
